chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Al-Fudayl who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman for one thousand dirhams, and then gave her a runaway slave of his and a silk garment worth one thousand dirhams, which was the dowry he gave her. He said: 'If she is pleased with the slave and she had known him, there is no harm if she takes possession of the garment and is pleased with the slave.' I said: 'And if he divorces her before consummating the marriage with her?' He said: 'She has no dowry, and she returns to him five hundred dirhams, and the slave remains hers.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.عَبْدًا لَهُ آبِقًا: A male slave who has run away

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry and financial settlement if a man divorces his wife before consummation when the dowry consisted of a slave and goods?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a dowry (mahr) can be composed of non-monetary assets like a slave and a garment, provided the wife explicitly accepts them. It establishes a specific legal precedent for pre-consummation divorce: the wife forfeits half the monetary value of the total dowry but retains the specific asset (the slave) already delivered to her, reflecting the Shia juristic view on partial forfeiture and asset retention.
